messages:
Alex Chen: Heads up — starting POC coordination for Orbis -> Redwood migration. Client: Argenta Bank. Need to align on API parity, prompt/response mapping, and security questionnaire. Can ops/devs chime in? TL;DR: tokenization differences, missing 'usage' field in Orbis responses, and KMS/SAML questions.

Maya Patel: On it. I can draft endpoint mapping and param parity. Can you drop a small Orbis sample request/response so I can map fields?

Alex Chen: Pasting minimal example from Argenta (redacted):
```http
POST /v1/generate
Body: {prompt: 'Summarize the following...', model: 'orbis-xl', max_tokens: 256}
Response: {text: '...', id: 'abc123', cost: 0.002}
```
They rely on 'cost' and 'id' semantics. Redwood uses token-based billing and 'request_id' naming.

Lucas Rivera: Pricing Q — client asked for delta vs Orbis for 100M tokens/mo. I have list price but need committed discount tiers and an estimate for reserved capacity. @Maya can you supply a rough estimate for same throughput?

Maya Patel: Yes. For 100M tokens with Dedicated reserved capacity we can propose a 20% commit discount + burst pricing. Quantization options reduce unit cost by ~35% but may affect latency. I'll share a formatted estimate to sales.

Sophia Nguyen: Security note: Argenta requires SOC 2 attestation, SAML SSO, BYOK/KMS, and VPC peering or private connectivity. We support SAML and customer KMS; VPC private preview is required and needs infra sign-off. Mark VPC peering as an enterprise blocker until approved.

Kevin Park: On parity: Orbis returns a top-level 'cost' and 'id' plus a 'usage' object with token counts. Redwood names the id field 'request_id' and reports token counts in metrics but not always in the response body. We can add a compatibility shim to map 'request_id'->'id' and inject a 'usage' object computed from token counters. Small latency hit (~10-20ms) expected. Also note Orbis tokenization treats certain unicode sequences differently — we'll normalize input in the shim.

Alex Chen: Canary plan proposal: 1) deploy compat shim to staging, 2) run prompt parity suite (100 representative prompts) and diff outputs + manual review, 3) load test at 50 rps for 24h, 4) collect latency and cost delta, 5) sign-off for production cutover.

Lucas Rivera: Customer also asked about rate-limit semantics. Orbis uses per-minute buckets and returns 429 with Retry-After header. Redwood uses per-second token buckets and returns 429 as well; Retry-After is seconds. We'll document mapping and fallback behavior.

Maya Patel: I'll create the mapping doc and a PR with a sample curl for their engs. Example curl for Redwood shim staging:
```bash
curl -X POST 'https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' \\
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \\
 -d '{\'prompt\': \'Summarize...\', \'max_tokens\': 256}'
```
(Using single quotes inside payload to avoid accidental quoting in their shell examples.)

ci-bot: deployer: staging-shim-deploy started by Maya Patel at 2024-09-18T14:02:21Z :rocket:

Sophia Nguyen: Follow-up Q for compliance team — does Redwood retain PII in logs by default? Argenta requires 30-day retention then purge. We have configurable retention windows but need ops to confirm purge job cadence and proof for their audit.

Kevin Park: I'll add a 'compat_mode' flag that flips mapping and adds legacy header support 'X-Orbis-Compat'. We'll also add an option to include a legacy 'usage' block in the response when compat_mode=true.

Alex Chen: :thumbsup: Ok next steps — Maya to send pricing estimate and mapping doc, Kevin to land shim in staging and add compat flag, Sophia to confirm VPC timeline and retention cadence, Lucas to update contract draft with commit discount proposal. I'll set a follow-up sync Thu 10am. Anyone blocked?

Maya Patel: Blocked by samples — need 10 complex prompts from their ML team to validate edge cases. @Lucas please ask them for the sample set.

Lucas Rivera: On it. Looping in Argenta ML team now (argenta-ml@argenta.com).
